name: Wispr Flow
tagline: AI voice dictation that turns natural speech into polished text in any app, on desktop and mobile.
description: Wispr Flow is a voice-to-text app that works system-wide on Mac, Windows, iPhone, and Android, converting speech into edited, formatted text inside any application. It removes filler words, adapts formatting to the app in use, supports 100+ languages, and learns a personal dictionary over time. It is used by writers, developers, lawyers, sales teams, and accessibility users who want to replace typing with speaking.
pricing_details: Flow Basic is free with weekly word limits (2,000 words/week on desktop, 1,000 on iPhone). Flow Pro is $15/user/mo or $12/user/mo billed annually with unlimited words; Enterprise is custom-priced with SOC 2 and SSO. New accounts get a 14-day Pro trial.
use_cases: Dictating emails, documents, and messages instead of typing
Voice input for coding tools like Cursor and VS Code
Drafting legal notes, case records, and client communications
Faster ticket and DM responses for support and sales teams
Accessibility-friendly text input for users slowed by keyboards
pros: Works in any app across Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android
AI auto-editing produces clean, formatted text without filler words
Personal dictionary, snippets, and 100+ language support
Genuine free tier plus a 14-day Pro trial
cons: Free plan has tight weekly word limits
Best results still require reviewing dictated text
Full compliance features (SOC 2, enforced HIPAA) gated to Enterprise
who_its_for: Writers and knowledge workers with heavy typing loads
Developers who want voice input in coding tools
Sales, support, and legal professionals
Users with accessibility needs
key_features: System-wide dictation in any application
AI auto-edits that clean up rambling speech
Command mode for voice-driven text editing
Personal dictionary and snippet shortcuts
100+ languages with automatic detection
Privacy mode with zero data retention

name: Superwhisper
tagline: Voice-to-text app with on-device AI models for private dictation on macOS, Windows, and iOS.
description: Superwhisper is an AI dictation app that runs Whisper models locally on the device, so audio never has to leave the user's machine, with optional cloud models for higher accuracy. Beyond dictation in any app, it offers file and meeting transcription, custom modes, and integrations aimed at driving agentic coding tools like Cursor and Claude Code by voice. It is built by an independent developer and popular with privacy-conscious professionals and developers.
pricing_details: Free tier includes unlimited use of small local models and voice-to-text in any app. Pro is listed by third-party sources at $8.49/mo, $84.99/yr, or a $249.99 lifetime license; the official pricing page was not directly fetchable at review time.
use_cases: Private, offline dictation for sensitive professional work
Voice prompting of AI coding agents like Cursor and Claude Code
Transcribing meetings and audio or video files
Writing long-form text faster than typing
Multilingual dictation and translation
pros: On-device processing keeps audio private by default
Choice of local and cloud AI models with custom modes
Usable free tier rather than a time-limited trial
Lifetime license option avoids a recurring subscription
cons: Local models are less accurate than the largest cloud models
Model downloads and settings can feel technical for casual users
Cloud model usage can add per-provider API costs
who_its_for: Privacy-conscious professionals such as lawyers and clinicians
Developers driving agentic coding tools by voice
Mac and iOS users who want offline dictation
Writers who prefer a one-time purchase option
key_features: System-wide dictation with on-device Whisper models
Optional cloud models for higher accuracy
Meeting recording and file transcription
Custom modes and per-app profiles
100+ languages with translation
Works with agentic coding apps

name: VoiceOS
tagline: Voice operating system for Mac and Windows that dictates text and executes actions across apps.
description: VoiceOS is a voice assistant for Mac and Windows that combines dictation with an agent layer: users can dictate text in any app, rewrite selected text by voice, and trigger multi-step actions such as sending Slack messages, replying to Gmail, or creating calendar events. Actions run across integrated apps with user confirmation before execution. It is built by WakoAI, a San Francisco startup backed by Y Combinator, and targets founders and professionals who want to replace repetitive keyboard work with voice commands.
pricing_details: 7-day free trial, then Pro at $11.99/month billed annually with unlimited usage. Enterprise is custom-priced with zero data retention, SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and SSO/SAML.
use_cases: Dictating polished text in any desktop application
Sending Slack messages and email replies by voice
Creating and moving calendar events hands-free
Asking questions about what is on screen
Rewriting selected text with voice commands
pros: Goes beyond dictation to executing real actions across apps
Works system-wide on both Mac and Windows
Confirmation step before any action is taken
Audio not stored on servers unless the user opts in
cons: No permanent free tier, only a 7-day trial
Agent integrations center on Google and Slack ecosystems
Young product with a smaller track record than established rivals
who_its_for: Founders and operators who live in Slack, Gmail, and Calendar
Voice-first professionals on Mac or Windows
Users who want one tool for dictation plus app actions
Teams needing enterprise controls on a voice assistant
key_features: Dictation mode with automatic formatting per app
Agent mode for multi-step actions across integrated apps
Edit mode for voice-driven rewriting
Screen-aware questions and answers
Privacy controls with on-device transcript storage option
Enterprise tier with SOC 2, ISO 27001, and SSO

name: Fyxer
tagline: AI email assistant that sorts the inbox, drafts replies in your tone, and takes meeting notes.
description: Fyxer connects to Gmail or Outlook and automatically categorizes incoming email, drafts replies matched to the user's writing tone, and records meetings to produce summaries and follow-ups. It works inside the existing inbox rather than requiring a new email client, and scales from individual professionals to large teams. The company is headquartered in New York and London and was founded by Richard Hollingsworth, Archie Hollingsworth, and Matthew Ffrench.
pricing_details: Starter is $22.50/user/month and Professional is $37.50/user/month, both billed annually ($30 and $50 month-to-month per third-party reviews); Enterprise is custom. A 7-day free trial is offered.
use_cases: Triaging a high-volume inbox into smart categories
Sending tone-matched reply drafts with minimal editing
Capturing meeting notes and follow-ups automatically
Searching email and meeting history for context
Standardizing email workflow across client-facing teams
pros: Works inside Gmail and Outlook with near-zero setup
Drafts learn the user's tone over time
Combines inbox triage, drafting, and meeting notes in one tool
SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, GDPR, and HIPAA compliance
cons: No free tier beyond a short trial
Does not support Apple Mail
Per-seat pricing adds up for larger teams
who_its_for: Professionals who spend 2+ hours a day on email
Sales, consulting, and real estate teams
Executives managing heavy meeting schedules
Organizations wanting a managed, compliant email assistant
key_features: Automatic inbox categorization and prioritization
Reply drafts written in the user's voice
Meeting recording, transcription, and summaries for online and in-person meetings
Fyxer Chat for searching email and meeting context
Scheduling suggestions and booking links in replies
CRM integration on the Professional plan

name: Jace
tagline: AI email agent that organizes the inbox and prepares context-rich reply drafts in your voice.
description: Jace is an AI email assistant that connects to a user's inbox, labels and prioritizes incoming mail, and prepares reply drafts that pull in context from attachments, calendar, and connected tools like Slack. It also supports custom automation rules and integrations that trigger actions in other business tools when email arrives. Jace is built by Zeta Labs, a London startup founded by former Meta engineers, and is aimed at professionals and teams with heavy email workloads.
pricing_details: 7-day free trial, then credit-based plans: Plus is $25/mo ($20/mo billed annually) for 10,000 monthly credits and 2 inboxes; Pro is $50/mo ($40/mo billed annually) starting at 20,000 credits and up to 8 inboxes. Enterprise is usage-based and custom.
use_cases: Reviewing pre-written reply drafts instead of composing from scratch
Auto-labeling and prioritizing a busy inbox
Pulling attachment, calendar, and Slack context into replies
Automating follow-up actions via custom rules
Triggering tickets and notifications from incoming email
pros: Drafts include context from attachments and connected tools
Self-onboarding with no manual training required
Flexible automation rules beyond simple drafting
Competitive entry price compared with similar email assistants
cons: Credit-based metering can be hard to predict
Gmail-centric; third-party reviewers note limited provider support
Occasionally generates drafts for low-value email
who_its_for: Founders and operators drowning in inbound email
Professionals who want drafts ready on inbox open
Teams connecting email to Slack and ticketing tools
Power users who want rule-based email automation
key_features: AI reply drafts with attachment and calendar context
Automatic labeling by type and priority
Custom smart rules for CCs, templates, and actions
Business integrations that trigger workflows from email
Chat over 1-3 years of email history
Support for multiple inboxes and unlimited calendars

name: Howie
tagline: Email-based AI secretary that schedules and reschedules meetings by handling the back-and-forth.
description: Howie is an AI scheduling secretary that works over email, SMS, and iMessage: users CC Howie on a thread and it negotiates times, sends invites, reschedules, and follows up until the meeting is booked. It learns individual scheduling preferences and manages calendars with a focus on doing one job - calendar management - rather than being a general assistant. The Seattle-based company raised a $6M seed round in 2025 and reports scheduling thousands of meetings per week for over a thousand paying customers.
pricing_details: The official site advertises Individual, Team, and custom Enterprise tiers with a free starting option, but does not publish exact prices; third-party comparisons cite Standard around $35/user/month and Pro around $145/user/month.
use_cases: Booking meetings by CC'ing Howie on an email thread
Coordinating group meetings across busy schedules
Rescheduling and clearing the calendar on short notice
Following up automatically when invitees go quiet
Enforcing personal scheduling preferences and focus time
pros: Handles the entire scheduling conversation end to end
Learns flexible, user-defined scheduling preferences
Works over email and messaging without a new app to learn
Deliberately narrow scope keeps it reliable at its one job
cons: Scheduling only - no broader email or task assistance
Exact pricing is not published on the official site
Historically centered on Google Calendar, limiting Outlook shops
who_its_for: Executives and founders with heavy external meeting loads
Sales and recruiting teams scheduling constantly
Professionals who want a human-like secretary experience
Teams replacing manual EA scheduling work
key_features: CC-based scheduling over email, SMS, and iMessage
Automatic follow-ups until meetings are booked
Rescheduling and conflict detection
Customizable scheduling preferences and rules
Calendar audits and focus-time protection
Team and Enterprise plans with custom billing and support

name: Littlebird
tagline: Ambient AI assistant that reads your screen and meetings so it already knows what you're working on.
description: Littlebird is a desktop AI assistant for Mac and Windows that builds a private memory of a user's work by observing the active window, listening to meetings, and connecting to tools like email and calendar. It uses that context to answer questions, take meeting notes, draft emails and documents in the user's voice, and run scheduled routines such as morning briefings. The San Francisco company launched publicly in late 2025 and raised an $11M seed round led by Lotus Studio.
pricing_details: Basic is free with daily usage credits and limited meeting notes. Plus is $17/mo billed annually ($20 monthly), Power is $42/mo billed annually ($50 monthly), and Pro starts at $100/mo; Team starts at $17/seat/mo and Enterprise is custom.
use_cases: Asking an assistant that already has context on current work
Automatic meeting notes and pre-meeting prep
Drafting emails and docs informed by real work context
Instant cross-app search over things seen on screen
Scheduled briefings and recurring routines
pros: Full work context without manual copy-pasting into a chatbot
User controls which apps are visible and can delete data anytime
SOC 2 certified with a no-training-on-your-data policy
Generous free tier and optional integrations
cons: Always-on screen observation will not suit every workplace
Heavier usage quickly pushes users into higher-priced tiers
Cloud storage of captured context requires trusting the vendor
who_its_for: Knowledge workers juggling many apps, docs, and meetings
Founders and managers who want automatic recall
Client-facing professionals needing meeting prep and notes
Users who want a personal assistant without manual setup
key_features: Screen-aware context across all apps without setup
Meeting notes in 10+ languages plus meeting prep
Cross-app instant search over observed work
Drafting in the user's voice from real context
Scheduled routines like daily briefings
Hundreds of optional integrations and MCP access on higher tiers

name: Stilla
tagline: AI teammate that turns conversations across meetings and tools into completed work.
description: Stilla is a collaborative AI platform that maintains shared memory across an organization's tools, meetings, and conversations, then acts on it - drafting PRs, posting Slack updates, editing Notion pages, and automating workflows across 3,000+ integrations. It includes AI meeting notes, a coding agent, sandboxed task machines, and an MCP server for extensibility. The Stockholm-based company was founded by Siavash Ghorbani and Kaj Drobin and emerged from stealth in early 2026 with $5M in funding.
pricing_details: Free to start with $100 in usage credits and no card required; ongoing use is credit-based. Detailed paid tier pricing is not published on the public site.
use_cases: Turning meeting outcomes into tasks and follow-ups automatically
Mentioning @Stilla in Slack or Discord to execute work
Automating workflows across 3,000+ connected tools
Delegating code changes to an agent that opens and reviews PRs
Searching shared memory across every connected tool
pros: Shared memory persists context across tools and conversations
Acts directly in tools rather than only suggesting next steps
Free starting credits with no card required
Open extensibility via MCP server
cons: Very new product with limited public track record
Credit-based pricing is not transparent on the site
Capped at 29 members per organization on standard plans
who_its_for: Product and engineering teams drowning in coordination work
Startups that want agentic automation without building it
Teams standardizing workflows as reusable skills
Organizations wanting one memory layer across their stack
key_features: Shared memory across tools, meetings, and chats
Agents that execute work in Slack, Discord, GitHub, and more
AI meeting notes with automatic tasks and follow-ups
Coding agent that writes, opens, and reviews PRs
3,000+ integrations plus an MCP server
Sandboxed computers for running tasks

name: Demi
tagline: Proactive AI teammate for Mac that drafts replies, books meetings, and clears to-dos before you ask.
description: Demi is a Mac app that works alongside the user, spotting to-dos across connected tools and preparing the actions to clear them - drafting email replies, booking meetings, summarizing threads, and updating CRM records. It shows each planned action for approval before executing, and connects to 100+ tools including Gmail, Google Calendar, Slack, and CRMs. It targets individuals and small teams who want a proactive assistant rather than a chatbot they have to prompt.
pricing_details: Individual plan is $50/month for the Mac app with upgradeable usage credits; Team pricing is custom with dedicated onboarding and compliance review support.
use_cases: Approving pre-drafted email replies instead of writing them
Booking meetings and managing calendar logistics
Summarizing long threads and teeing up follow-ups
Keeping the CRM updated from daily work
Delegating tasks from any app or screen on Mac
pros: Proactively surfaces tasks instead of waiting for prompts
Approval gate on every action before anything is sent
Broad 100+ tool connectivity including CRM and Drive
Google-verified app with SOC 2 Type II and CASA Tier II compliance
cons: Mac-only at present
No free tier; $50/month entry is steep for casual users
Messaging channels beyond Slack (iMessage, WhatsApp) still upcoming
who_its_for: Busy executives and founders on Mac
Sales and customer-facing professionals
Individuals who want delegation rather than a chatbot
Small teams standardizing on one assistant

Drafted replies, meeting booking, and thread summaries
Human approval required before any action executes
100+ integrations including Gmail, Calendar, Slack, and CRMs
